title: Deal Focus: Netflix in biggest live sports rights move to date
article_text:
Last week, content and streaming giant Netflix made its biggest splash in the world of live sports rights yet, through a deal to cover soccer’s 2030 men’s FIFA World Cup in joint-host nation Spain.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Netflix will air all 104 games from the 48-team tournament live, and will also make a selection – one game per matchday – available free-to-air. This number will include all of Spain’s fixtures – with the team having won the 2026 World Cup earlier this year – as well as both semi-finals and the tournament final.

Spain will co-host the 2030 men’s soccer tournament alongside Portugal and Morocco, while Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay will all stage one game each.

The deal was struck directly with soccer’s global governing body FIFA.

It is reportedly likely that Netflix will seek a sub-licensing deal for the aforementioned one free game per matchday, instead of offering up that fixture without payment itself.

For Netflix, this is the culmination of a lengthy run-up in terms of its sports rights acquisition policy.

In terms of soccer rights, it adds to the content heavyweight’s deal covering both the 2027 and 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cups, struck in late 2024 and extending across the US and Canada.

This latest agreement marks the first time Netflix will air the men's World Cup – soccer's national team pinnacle – in any market, and it is making its debut in the winning nation from the previous edition.

Netflix is also set to air the Gold Cup and Concacaf Nations League Finals men’s national team competitions in Mexico (one of the competing countries). Under a four-year agreement, Netflix will have exclusive rights there to the 2027 and 2029 editions of both competitions.

It has also been rapidly expanding its live rights presence in a range of other sports over the past 18 months – including in American football, baseball, boxing, mixed martial arts, and wrestling.

Regarding its existing presence as a sports broadcaster in Spain, this agreement represents its first live rights tie-up of any significance in that major soccer market.

Up until this point, it has been limited to airing sports-centric documentaries to a Spanish audience, with Spanish-themed documentaries including one on Luis Figo, an iconic player for soccer heavyweights Real Madrid and Barcelona. It is also airing a behind-the-scenes documentary on the country's LaLiga top domestic soccer property.

Peter Scrimgeour, senior analyst at GlobalData Sport, explains: "This is a landmark European sports rights acquisition for Netflix and a clear indication that its targeted live-sports strategy is gaining momentum. The Spanish rights were likely to attract intense competition given the country’s status as a principal 2030 host nation and the tournament’s significant domestic appeal. Spain being the current men's World Cup champions would further support a premium valuation for the package.

"The deal also fits Netflix’s broader sports strategy of prioritizing localized or global tentpole events over season-long packages. Its portfolio now spans the World Baseball Classic in Japan, the FIFA Women’s World Cup in the US and Canada, Concacaf properties in Mexico, WWE’s Raw, MLB’s Opening Night, and NFL Christmas Day games. These events give Netflix high-impact opportunities to acquire subscribers, reduce churn, and grow advertising revenue without entering into long-term agreements and committing to the cost and operational complexity of a full sports season.”

During the 2030 World Cup, Netflix will air pre-game, halftime, and post-game shows, a daily roundup program on each matchday, as well as additional preview content during the immediate build-up to the tournament.

The tournament in four years' time will take place across 11 Spanish stadia, three venues in Portugal, and six in Morocco (as well as one each in the aforementioned trio of South American nations).

In Spain, Netflix currently costs between €9 and €21 monthly.

title: FIFA launches tender of 2030 men's World Cup U.S. media rights, plans to choose winner by end of year
article_text:
The FIFA men's World Cup U.S. television rights are formally up for auction.

FIFA is launching its tender offer Thursday for the 2030 U.S. media rights with an option for potential partners to also buy rights for the 2034 World Cup. FIFA wants bids in by Nov. 19.

YouTube, Netflix, Amazon and Disney are all interested, CNBC reported in July. Rights could sell for between $1.5 billion and $2 billion, some media executives predicted at the time. FIFA hasn't sold U.S. men's World Cup TV rights since 2011.

Fox paid $425 million for the 2026 World Cup, which broke U.S. ratings records. Matches averaged 13.5 million viewers — up 166% from 2022.

The 2030 World Cup will take place in Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

FIFA would prefer to sell the English and the Spanish-language rights packaged together to one media partner – a departure from previous deals. For this past World Cup, NBCUniversal's Telemundo owned the Spanish rights while Fox owned the English rights. That led to some tension between the broadcasters and FIFA, as Peacock carried the Spanish-language rights for a less expensive price than Fox One, which streamed the games with English announcers.

FIFA Chief Business Officer Romy Gai said it's too early to gauge what price is realistic for the 2030 World Cup. FIFA is willing to listen to offers where just one media company buys the entire package or a joint offering – potentially between a streamer and a traditional broadcaster.

"We want to be flexible," said Gai in an interview. "We expect a big number of participants, both from the linear side and from the streamer side, but we want to listen to what is relevant for them, and then we can build up the best case together."

While the 2026 World Cup took place in the U.S., Canada and Mexico — allowing matches to be played during U.S. afternoons and nights — the 2030 World Cup will have a significant time difference. The 2034 World Cup will be played in Saudi Arabia. Riyadh is seven hours ahead of New York.

The time zones may make it difficult for games to be played during U.S. primetime hours. That will play a role in how much media companies are willing to spend on both tournaments, but Gai doesn't expect the time zone challenges to play too much of a role in the bidding.

"I'm sure that we will have every day matches that will be available in the right time zone for the U.S.," Gai said. "We expect it to have an impact [on the bidding], but not as big as you think."

If a streaming service wins the rights, FIFA will ensure that a certain number of matches are available for free, either by forcing the streamer to sublicense certain rights or by putting some games on a free version of the service, if such a thing exists.

Netflix has already acquired the 2030 World Cup rights in Spain. That deal allows a free-to-air broadcaster to show at least one game each day.

After Nov. 19, when bids are due, a contingent from FIFA will come to the U.S. around Thanksgiving and begin speaking with media companies in person, Gai said. At that point, FIFA could narrow down the field and ask for one more final bid – or it could just choose a winner.

FIFA intends to select its next media partner before the end of the year, said Gai.

Hahn Secures Multi-Year Partnership as Official Beer of the Australian Open
article_text:
Tennis Australia has significantly bolstered its commercial partner portfolio ahead of the upcoming summer of tennis, announcing a major multi-year agreement with beverage giant LION that positions Hahn as the Official Beer of the Australian Open.

Announced on 22 October 2026, the strategic alliance is set to transform hospitality and spectator engagement across Melbourne Park when the tournament kicks off from 11 to 31 January 2027. At the commercial epicentre of the partnership is the construction of Hahn House, a vibrant two-storey destination situated on Grand Slam Oval. Designed to act as one of the precinct’s premier social hubs, the customised venue features an expansive beer garden layout offering patrons direct access to the festival atmosphere surrounding the tournament.

Beyond Hahn’s marquee activation, the multiple brand partnership extends LION’s market presence across the entire sporting precinct. Stone & Wood will infuse its signature coastal atmosphere into Garden Square, while Four Pillars will curate an exclusive experience at Kia Arena. Furthermore, the collaboration incorporates nationwide consumer initiatives, including limited edition product packaging, sports merchandise, and interactive community programs featuring pop-up pickleball courts across Australia.

The partnership was engineered to elevate fan spend and enhance the broader hospitality ecosystem of the grand slam, aligning world class sport with premier beverage brands. Tennis Australia Chief Commercial Officer Cedric Cornelis underscored the strategic alignment between the sporting organisation and the beverage manufacturer.

“The Australian Open is where world-class sport, entertainment, hospitality and culture come together, and LION is a brand that shares our passion for bringing people together to celebrate great moments.

“We are constantly looking for new ways to elevate the fan experience, and Hahn House will provide an exciting new destination on Grand Slam Oval where fans can soak up the atmosphere, enjoy great hospitality and stay connected to every moment of the action,” Cornelis said.

Echoing these commercial sentiments, LION Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director Anubha Sahasrabuddhe highlighted the broader brand investment value of aligning with Australia’s premier summer sporting spectacle.

“Partnering with Tennis Australia is a major milestone for LION as we continue to invest in Australia’s biggest cultural and sporting moments.

“The Australian Open sets the global benchmark for major events, and there is no better backdrop to share the love on and off the court, showcasing our portfolio through elevated hospitality experiences.

“We are looking forward to working closely with Tennis Australia to deliver the best guest experience possible across Melbourne Park and beyond during the Summer of Tennis.” Sahasrabuddhe said.

With ticket sales already moving swiftly via Ticketmaster and corporate hospitality demand surging, the Hahn partnership reinforces the Australian Open’s standing as a premier commercial platform for leading consumer brands.

title: Ashmita Chaliha Stuns Three-Time World Champion Akane Yamaguchi At French Open
article_text:
Ashmita Chaliha produced the biggest victory of her career, stunning world champion and third seed Akane Yamaguchi in straight games to reach the French Open quarterfinals.

Star Indian women’s singles shuttler Ashmita Chaliha, who won the Korea Masters earlier this year, stunned the 2025 World Championships gold medallist and third seed Akane Yamaguchi in the second round of the French Open to pull off the biggest win of her career.

Ashmita, who had beaten China’s Han Qian Xi in a 21-18, 24-22 first-round thriller on Tuesday, beat Yamaguchi in yet another close match, winning 21-19, 21-18.

Ashmita was the underdog coming into this clash, having lost to the Japanese shuttler last week in the Round of 16 of the Denmark Open in what was their first-ever clash on tour.

But Ashmita took just a week to avenge the defeat, stunning Yamaguchi and ending her hopes of winning a fourth French Open title.

Ashmita will either face 11th seed Pornpawee Chochuwong or Nozomi Okuhara in the quarterfinal.

Much like the Denmark Open last week, the French Open has been yet another disappointing outing for Indian shuttlers and Ashmita’s big win might come as a breath of fresh air for many.

On Tuesday, the opening day of the tournament, World Championships bronze medallists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand suffered a straight-game loss to a lower-ranked pair from Chinese Taipei.

Meanwhile, fifth seeds Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty extended their inconsistent run, going down in three games to the Popov brothers.

India endured another disappointing day on Wednesday as Unnati Hooda fell in three games to Riko Gunji, while Devika Sihag lost a three-game battle against fifth seed Putri Kusuma Wardani.

Lakshya Sen, meanwhile, conceded a walkover to sixth seed Kodai Naraoka.

India’s struggles continued on Thursday before Ashmita’s big victory over Yamaguchi, with Tanvi Sharma suffering a straight-game loss to top seed An Se-young, while Ayush Shetty retired during his match against Naraoka.

The only other bright spot for India was double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu’s straight-game win against Gunji. She will face either Chiu Pin-Chian or Sim Yu Jin in the quarterfinals.

title: CBS adds Spanish-language CONCACAF Champions Cup rights
article_text:
Paramount-owned US broadcaster CBS Sports has consolidated coverage of the CONCACAF Champions Cup regional club tournament, acquiring the Spanish-language rights to add to the English-language rights it already held.

This new deal will run through the 2030 campaign, as will the English-language package, meaning that the Paramount+ OTT streaming service will showcase all 51 CONCACAF Champions Cup games each year in both English and Spanish.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

In addition to Paramount+, select CONCACAF Champions Cup games will air for free in Spanish (and English) on the CBS Sports app.

CBS supplants rival TUDN, the Spanish-language channel in the US owned by Mexican media business TelevisaUnivision, which has broadcast the tournament for a number of years.

The Champions Cup is the region’s premier men’s club competition, featuring the best clubs from North America, Central America, and the Caribbean.

The tournament was established in 1962 and ran in its original incarnation with several format changes through 2008, when it was retitled the CONCACAF Champions League. It then returned to its Champions Cup moniker ahead of the 2024 edition.

Since its inception, the CONCACAF Champions Cup ha been dominated by Mexican sides, who have won all but one of the last 21 editions going back to 2006, and 40 of the 60 editions in all.

Much of the Spanish-speaking community in the US (and indeed the audience for Telemundo) stems from the country’s large Mexican diaspora, which accounts for as much as 11.2% of the population and close to 60% of all Hispanic US citizens.

As such, adding Spanish-language rights to the existing English-language ones, and thus bringing Spanish-language coverage of well-supported Mexican sides like Club America and Tigres to diaspora fans, could bring strong viewership for CBS.

Paramount’s soccer portfolio in the US also includes Europe’s elite UEFA Champions League club competition and rights to the English Football League, the organizer of the second, third, and fourth tiers of the country’s soccer league pyramid.

Earlier this year, CBS Sports landed rights to major competitions organized by the Asian Football Confederation until 2028.

Additionally, it renewed its deal to show Italy’s top-tier Serie A for another season and snapped up England's Women's Super League on a four-year deal.

title: Inside the Circle x Chelsea FC partnership
article_text:
The latest episode of The Game Plan explores why Circle chose Chelsea FC, what brands really want from football sponsorship, and why the strongest partnerships are about far more than logo placement.

Football sponsorship has never been more competitive, yet brands continue to invest heavily in some of the sport’s biggest assets.

On the latest episode of The Game Plan, Anna-Rose Gabbitass sits down with Kash Razzaghi, Chief Commercial Officer at Circle, to discuss the company’s decision to become Chelsea FC’s Principal Partner and front-of-shirt sponsor.

The conversation uses the partnership as a lens to examine a broader question facing the industry: what are brands actually looking for from football sponsorship in 2026?

Razzaghi explains why football’s global reach made it the natural platform for Circle’s ambitions, how the company evaluated one of the most visible sponsorship opportunities in sport, and why Chelsea stood out from the many organisations it considered.

While front-of-shirt sponsorships are often judged on visibility alone, Razzaghi argues that the most effective partnerships are built on much deeper foundations.

“We felt like we were going into this holding hands, jumping in, and we were going to figure things out together,” says Razzaghi.

The episode also explores the growing importance of authentic partnerships, the opportunity presented by both the men’s, women’s and academy games, and why organisations increasingly expect commercial relationships to extend far beyond traditional sponsorship models.

Elsewhere, listeners will hear how Circle plans to measure success in the early stages of the partnership, why the company believes football remains one of the most powerful global marketing platforms, and what the deal could tell us about the future direction of the sponsorship market.

The reason Jack Draper is currently playing tennis in Brazil with Joao Fonseca
article_text:
Jack Draper’s absence from the ATP Tour of late has been an expected one, given all the fitness troubles he’s suffered in recent years.

And, given the specific nature of his current injury, the only real antidote is rest.

For a professional athlete, that is nearly impossible to do, and tennis is arguably even worse.

With no security and a ranking system that benefits the ever-present, Jack Draper has suffered both financially and in terms of his stature: the Brit currently sits outside the world’s top 150.

Who is to blame for Jack Draper’s injury issues?

However, it seems that whatever recovery plan he and his team agreed on has reached its next step, with reports now emerging that he is back on court.

It’s not just reports that have confirmed Draper’s return to on-court action, with photos and videos also surfacing.

The 24-year-old has been pictured training in Rio, Brazil, at the same country club where Joao Fonseca started playing tennis.

In fact, the Brazilian youngster is apparently there now as well, with one update claiming his plan is to ‘get in shape physically and tennis-wise for next year.’

They added: “He also wants to build up his tolerance to high temperatures.”

Fonseca has also ended his season early, as part of a growing list of players struck down by injury. He was seen at the same club on Tuesday, although pictures of him and Draper together remain unreleased.

What is particularly interesting about this decision is not the timing of his return, but where he has chosen to return.

After all, opting to return to practice on clay courts seems odd with the Australian Open likely his ultimate target after taking so long off.

Even if he were to miss that first Grand Slam of the year, the clay-court season does not start until April, assuming he does play any events during the Golden Swing in Brazil and Argentina, across February.

Naturally, the warm weather seems to be his focus, but that could have been achieved on any surface. The clay must have been a conscious choice, and a curious one at that.

title: Badminton: Sindhu storms into BWF French Open semifinals
article_text:
Paris, October 23 (IANS) Indian badminton ace and two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu sailed into the semifinal of the BWF French Open, beating Chinese Taipei’s Chiu Pin-Chian 21-13, 21-14 in Paris on Friday.

The Indian made a good start, winning the first game 21-13. She took that momentum into the second game and led 11-2 at the interval. Chiu showed signs of fightback, but Sindhu closed out the win, taking the game 21-14.

Sindhu, who won a silver medal in the 2016 Rio Olympic Games followed by a bronze at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, will next meet either fifth seed Putri Wardani of Indonesia or Hina Akechi of Japan for a place in the final.

Earlier, Sindhu comfortably saw off Japan’s Riko Gunji 21-12, 21-16 in 44 minutes to advance. Notably, Gunji had knocked out Unnati Hooda in the opening round.

Meanwhile, Ashmita Chaliha's dream run came to an end as the youngster fell 10-21, 21-17, 16-21 to Japan's Nozomi Okhuhara in the quarterfinals on Friday.

Chaliha was enjoying a memorable week as she claimed the biggest victory of her career, a 21-19, 21-18 win over world No.3 Akane Yamaguchi to reach her maiden Super 750 quarterfinal on Thursday.

Having lost to Yamaguchi just a week earlier in Denmark, Chaliha had a different mindset in Paris. The world No. 36 Indian, who won her maiden BWF World Tour title at the Korea Masters Super 300 earlier this year, drew confidence from her previous encounter and was better prepared to deal with one of Yamaguchi’s most dangerous shots.

Meanwhile, Ayush Shetty’s campaign ended in the men’s singles when he retired hurt against sixth seed Kodai Naraoka of Japan, having lost the opening game 21-17 and trailing 11-6 in the second.

Ayush Shetty had beaten Kidambi Srikanth in the opening round of this year’s French Open. Lakshya Sen had withdrawn ahead of his opening-round match.

Satwiksairaj Rankireddy-Chirag Shetty and Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand had also suffered opening-round exits in Paris.

title: Analysis: MLB’s Regional Broadcast Rights Worth $1.6B Bespite TV Disruption
article_text:
MLB regional broadcast rights are currently worth $1.6bn, according to the latest Ampere estimates, accounting for 43% of the league’s total $3.7bn broadcast rights revenue. Rooted in linear cable, regional sports networks (RSNs) have come under increasing pressure from cord-cutting, as US households move away from traditional pay TV towards streaming.

Over the past four years, 13 of MLB’s 30 teams have lost their regional sports network partners, including 12 following the bankruptcies of Diamond Sports and Main Street Sports Group. This has been exacerbated by the decline in US pay TV, with Ampere estimating a drop in the market from 96 million US pay TV households in 2016 to 65 million by the end of 2026. Meanwhile, streaming households are anticipated to increase from 57 million to 112 million over the same period.

title: Son of Wallabies great named in spring tour squad as Les Kiss turns to new faces
article_text:
Son of a gun Teddy Wilson and prop Tom Lambert are the new faces in the Wallabies’ spring tour squad, which welcomes back some international reinforcements.

Coach Les Kiss on Friday unveiled his 33-man group to tour Europe for Tests next month against England, Scotland, Wales and another yet-to-be-determined side in the maiden Nations Championship finals weekend.

NSW scrumhalf and former Australian under-20s captain Wilson is the son of Wallabies great David Wilson, with the flanker part of the 1999 World Cup-winning side among his 79 caps.

“There’s a few [Wallabies] jerseys up at home, the 1999 World Cup winning jersey’s there as well,” Wilson said. “Dad, he’s been there and done that so he tells me a few things but lets me play my game.”

“[The main advice was to] just work hard. He was always that type of player and … if we were slacking off when I was younger he’d get us down to the oval, doing extras.”

Wilson was in superb form as Easts won Sydney’s Shute Shield competition and has vowed to back his running game if given a shot at Test level.

He has replaced Kalani Thomas as the third No 9 with the latter playing Australia A this weekend against the United States.

Ryan Lonergan has established himself as the standout No 9, with Wilson to push fellow tourist Tate McDermott in the battle to support him.

The Wallabies had gone six Tests undefeated, including Kiss’s first five in charge, before back-to-back Bledisloe Cup hidings opened old wounds.

Taniela Tupou and Tom Hooper, who play club rugby in France and England respectively, performed crucial bench roles in the Wallabies’ defeat of back-to-back World Cup champions South Africa.

But Australia were without the pair’s services against New Zealand, given the All Blacks Tests fell outside of World Rugby’s global player release period.

It exposed the Wallabies’ bench depth and, after a one-sided second half in Auckland, forced Kiss to shift prop Angus Bell to the reserves for the Sydney rematch.

That contest was over inside 30 minutes, before Bell got on the field.

Kiss will have access to his international arsenal though for the four-Test tour that begins in London on 9 November.

Flyhalf Carter Gordon is recovering from a fractured leg and has been included alongside Ben Donaldson and Declan Meredith, with Harry McLaughlin-Phillips squeezed out following his debut off the bench in Sydney.

Kiss has also included Japan-based Hunter Paisami, who was suspended for the Bledisloe Cup for a high tackle and lock Miles Amatosero, who will also play for Australia A in the US.

NSW junior, loosehead Lambert – who will join the Queensland Reds this season – has replaced Aidan Ross, who started against New Zealand in Sydney, in the squad.

Unused fullback Jock Campbell has also missed a spot on the plane.

Kiss said ahead of the Sydney Test that he had been in conversation with veteran playmaker Kurtley Beale who, like fellow experienced halves James O’Connor and Bernard Foley, was a known quantity who remained in the frame ahead of the World Cup.

“There’s a real buzz among the squad as we prepare for what will be four incredibly demanding matches against high-quality opposition,” Kiss said.

“We’ve made some tough selection calls to keep building depth across the board and we know a tour like this will challenge the whole squad on many levels.”

title: WRU says £18m loss shows why regional team must be axed
article_text:
The Welsh Rugby Union has spelled out the "tough" economic state of the game in Wales - despite suggesting its financial position was "pretty good" just five months ago.

The governing body has announced a significant decline in its finances, saying it has posted an £18m loss for the financial year to June 2026 - compared to a £7.2m loss the previous year.

Financial boss Gavin Marshall admitted the figures were disappointing and came despite turnover rising £10m to £116.2m.

Just five months ago, new chief financial and operating officer Marshall claimed the WRU's finances were in a "pretty good position".

But it says that rising energy and staffing costs, combined with falling ticket sales and reduced fan spend, were to blame for the dramatic fall.

The union says it is already predicting a similar loss next year, and said the figures back up its case that four professional regions are no longer sustainable.

"We can't go on like this," said Marshall.

The financial performance of the WRU, on the back of the controversial decision to cut the number of regions from four to three, is sure to provoke dismay, frustration and even anger from clubs and fans.

"The numbers are tough and not where we want them to be, but it's been a challenging year," said Marshall.

"As an executive team we are accountable for these numbers, so we have to look at our performance and where we can do better.

"But we can only control certain things and it's a tough world out there impacting all sport with the cost of living crisis affecting what people spend as well as our own costs.

"We should be aiming to break even but we're quite some way off where we want to be. I'm ambitious and we need to grow our way out of that deficit but the gap, right now, is stark."

The WRU insists Welsh rugby is "living beyond its means" and cannot go on sustaining such losses.

The official accounts for the past financial year are expected to be lodged with Companies House on Friday but have already been shared with clubs.

The WRU's audited annual report for the 2023 financial year showed new profit and loss figures for the previous two years, with the loss in 2023 re-listed as £14m up from £4.9m - although the profit in 2022 now stood at £37.3m rather than £2.9m.

Since that re-audited positive 2022 figure, the financial situation has continued to decline.

When former WRU chair Richard Collier-Keywood and a new board took charge at the start of 2024, he admitted the finances were "a mess".

In an interview with the BBC the following year he revealed the extent of the problem, saying that "in January 2024 the WRU had run out of money - we were up against our overdraft limit".

The WRU had taken out an £18m Covid support loan from the Welsh government in 2022, for which it subsequently appealed for an improvement in terms.

But a new £55m debt-refinancing package agreed in January 2026 - via banks HSBC and Goldman Sachs - was designed to see the Welsh government loan and a separate commercial loan paid off.

In the past few years, the union has also paid out £1.9m to departing employees, as well as keeping Cardiff afloat since taking over the struggling region in April 2025.

The WRU will struggle to avoid the accusation from west Wales that the regions threatened with closure - Ospreys and Scarlets, who have been approached for comment - are paying the price for the WRU's financial performance.

"We have a lot of costs, including the stadium [£26m], the national teams [£20m], interest on our loan [£3m], funding community rugby [£4m]," said Marshall.

"That leaves about £20m to invest in professional rugby but at the moment we're funding £26m across the four clubs. From a financial perspective, we just can't afford that.

"We need to grow revenue but also sensibly manage our costs, investments and distribution of funds.

"We could have as many clubs as you want but it's how you fund those clubs, how competitive they can be with that funding and how much benefactor funding goes into the clubs. At the moment we're not sustainable."

The men's national team is the biggest driving factor behind the WRU's revenue, contributing almost half its income.

So it is clear that while a successful Wales boosts the coffers, a team on a record losing run, as Steve Tandy's side were until March, sees income stall.

Empty seats for last year's home Test against world champions South Africa and again in the Six Nations game against France reflected a declining appetite among fans who, on average, are also spending less when they do attend the Principality Stadium.

"We hosted seven men's internationals compared with five the previous year but match income increased by only £2m," said Marshall.

"This was challenging and reflected lower average ticket prices, some lower attendances and the global economic pressure on consumer spending."

The WRU is now caught between encouraging more fans to buy tickets - broadening the price categories from three to six - and the need to maximise income from those key matches.

Adding fuel to the fire from west Wales is the WRU sustaining Cardiff's £1.2m loss for the past financial year.

That figure is not startling given Ospreys and Scarlets both lost more the previous year - the most recent figures on record.

title: All Blacks legend Sonny Bill Williams undergoes life-saving surgery
article_text:
All Blacks legend Sonny Bill Williams has revealed he underwent life-saving open-heart surgery after doctors discovered a serious heart defect.

The 41-year-old shared his ordeal in an emotional 24-minute YouTube video titled My Heart Stopped.

Doctors warned Williams that his heart had grown to 7.5cm and was at risk of rupturing.

“So, if I didn’t go in and get it checked, they wouldn’t know,” Williams explained.

He added that a person could look perfectly healthy before suddenly dropping dead.

Williams underwent surgery in Melbourne, with wife Alana documenting parts of his recovery.

The two-time Rugby World Cup winner admitted the days that followed were terrifying.

“It’s the hardest thing I’ve ever done. Day two, honestly, I thought I wasn’t going to make it.”

He also revealed that he suffered hallucinations following the operation.

Surgeon Dr Michael O’Keefe confirmed Williams had undergone a Ross procedure to replace his aortic valve.

Remarkably, doctors believe the condition may have affected his sporting career for years.

Williams said he had struggled with his fitness from his late twenties.

Thankfully, the operation was successful, with doctors telling him his heart now works more efficiently.

He won 58 Test caps for New Zealand between 2010 and 2019.

Williams won NRL titles with Canterbury Bulldogs in 2004 and Sydney Roosters in 2013.

He represented New Zealand in rugby sevens at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

Williams also enjoyed a professional boxing career, winning the WBA International heavyweight title in 2013.

title: Alcaraz sails through Shanghai opener, Auger-Aliassime & Fritz also advance
article_text:
The Spanish star, seeded second, put on a dominant show to brush aside the 55th-ranked Argentinian in the second round in just 66 minutes.

"Really, really happy with the way I played today. It wasn't easy," said the 23-year-old former number one.

"Just had two days of preparation... I came from Tokyo, there were totally different conditions," he added. "Just tried to play the best that I can."

Sporting a fresh moustache, Alcaraz signed a camera "Moustache Team" following his win.

Asked by an on-court interviewer about the new look, Alcaraz said: "It's gonna stay."

He will play either Ignacio Buse or Zizou Bergs in the next round.

World number five Felix Auger-Aliassime also survived a scare, needing three hours to beat 77th-ranked Camilo Ugo Carabelli 4-6, 7-6(1), 7-5.

The Canadian will play Spaniard Pablo Carreno-Busta in the third round.

Several matches in the afternoon were suspended due to rain, but Taylor Fritz, Casper Ruud and Arthur Fils all went through as play resumed.

title: PV Sindhu Reaches French Open 2026 Semifinals; Ashmita Chaliha Exits
article_text:
Indian badminton star PV Sindhu delivered a masterclass in control and aggression, cruising into the semifinals of the French Open Super 750 with a clinical straight-game victory over Chinese Taipei’s Chiu Pin-Chian on October 23.

Sindhu, who is chasing her second BWF World Tour title of the season following her Japan Open triumph earlier this year, completely dominated the match. Displaying her trademark fierce attacking calibre, blistering round-the-head smashes, and a rock-solid defence, the two-time Olympic medallist dispatched Chiu 21-13, 21-14 to keep her quest for a maiden French Open title alive.

Sindhu’s journey to the final four has tested both her tactical acumen and mental fortitude. In the Round of 32, she survived a major scare against Thailand’s Supanida Katethong. After cruising through a comfortable opening, Sindhu squandered a commanding 19-8 lead in the decider as Katethong staged a sensational comeback to level at 20-20. Breaking her recent pattern of closing-stage jitters, Sindhu held her nerve to clinch a tense 23-21 thriller. She followed that up with a much smoother straight-games win (21-12, 21-16) against Japan’s Riko Gunji in the Round of 16.

With her latest victory, Sindhu stands as the last remaining Indian contender in the tournament. In the semifinals, she will square off against the winner of the quarterfinal clash between Indonesia’s Putri Kusuma Wardani and Japan’s Hina Aakechi. Should she advance to the title clash, a potential blockbuster final against World No. 1 An Se Young—who faces Nozomi Okuhara in the opposite half—could await.

While Sindhu marched forward, compatriot Ashmita Chaliha saw her fairytale run in Paris come to an end. Chaliha had sent shockwaves through the tournament earlier by stunning World No. 2 and three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi in a brilliant straight-games victory (21-19, 21-18).

In the quarterfinals, Chaliha pushed former world champion Nozomi Okuhara to the absolute limit before bowing out 10-21, 21-17, 16-21. Despite the loss, Chaliha leaves Paris with her head held high after a stellar performance that turned heads on the global stage.

title: Golfer on the verge of tears as DP World Tour withdrawal has major consequences
article_text:
Kiradech Aphibarnrat was visibly emotional after withdrawing from the Genesis Championship - which meant he lost his DP World Tour card for 2027.

The Thai golf star needed a big result at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club in South Korea to keep his card for the 2027 season.

Aphibarnrat began the week in 106th in the Race to Dubai Rankings - the season-long competition on the DP World Tour.

However, only players inside the top 100 are guaranteed Category 10 status - which automatically secures their membership on the DP World Tour for next year.

The Genesis Championship is the final event before season-ending play-off events at Yas Links in Abu Dhabi and then Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai.

This meant that Aphibarnrat required a strong showing to give himself a chance of making either event to then boost his ranking.

Unfortunately for Aphibarnrat, he found himself up against it in South Korea after shooting a four-over 75 in his first round.

And it all proved too much for him in round two on Friday when he found himself five-over-par just nine holes in.

Knowing he would struggle to claw anything back, the 37-year-old made the difficult decision to withdraw - ending his chances of keeping his tour card automatically.

This left Aphibarnrat visibly upset, and he fought back tears in an interview afterwards as he shared his disappointment.

He told the DP World Tour: “First of all, I just have to apologise. I really let them (the fans) down.

"There’s not many times in my life that I have disappointed people, especially my family and all the fans.

“In the last 15 years I’ve had a really good career but just the last three or four years haven’t been easy. I’m a fighter so I believe I’m going to get past all of this and we’ll come back strong.”

While Aphibarnrat couldn't hide his disappointment over failing to keep his tour card via ranking, he shared his hopes of sealing an instant return at Qualifying School in Spain next month.

The entertaining golfer has come through Q School before, having won his card back in successive years in 2022 and 2023.

He explained: "Yesterday going out and the game was not as good as I expected, so I worked quite hard after the round.

"And this morning I felt jammed a little bit, but I had to go out and try, but at some point I just felt like the body just couldn't move and couldn't answer what I needed it to do.

"It's quite a disappointing result, but it is what it is.

"I've got my tour card back twice on Q School, I need to go back there again and who knows, it might be my best year next season."

Aphibarnrat has previously reached a career-high PGA Tour ranking of world no.29 in 2018.

His best results at major championships came at the 2016 Masters and the 2018 US Open - where he finished T15 on both occasions.

However, the Asian golf star has struggled to replicate this form in recent years, and his last major appearance came at the 2019 Open Championship - famously won by Shane Lowry.

But with Aphibarnrat now struggling for ranking points on the DP World Tour, he admitted playing 11 straight weeks in a bid to retain his full playing privileges had left him drained this week.

He added: "It's really difficult. The last 10 weeks were so tough, I made the cut on the number many times so I feel like on the mental part I'm working twice as hard as everybody else.

"My game was not quite there so I was trying hard from the first hole to the last one on the second day to make sure I make the cut.

"So every week after the round I felt like I didn't have any gas left in the tank."

title: Four-time DP World Tour winner apologizes to fans as he loses card for 2027, 'I really let them down'
article_text:
As the DP World Tour season begins to wind down, numerous players face the prospect of losing their cards this year.

It is back to qualifying school for those who finished outside the top 100 bubble after the Genesis Championship.

Obviously there are still a few events to be played, but those who finish outside the top 100 this week in South Korea will lose their cards.

What was the event that got you hooked on golf?

How did you end up falling in love with the game?

Some big names fell victim to exactly that this week, including popular Thai player Kiradech Aphibarnrat.

The 37-year-old missed the cut this week in South Korea and will now be forced to go back to Q-school in order to try and earn back his DP World Tour card.

Aphibarnrat was visibly upset after he was forced to retire from the Genesis Championship with a back injury on Friday.

The man from Thailand spoke honestly about his recent struggles after leaving the golf course due to a back issue.

“First of all, I just have to apologise. I really let them (the fans) down,“ he said.

“There’s not many times in my life that I have disappointed people, especially my family and all the fans.

“In the last 15 years I’ve had a really good career but just the last three or four years haven’t been easy. I’m a fighter so I believe I’m going to get past all of this and we’ll come back strong.”

Of course, Aphibarnrat has absolutely nothing to apologise for. He has tried his best over the past few months to claw his way back inside the top 100 in the standings.

However, as is sometimes the case in golf, the harder he has worked on his game, the worse his results have become.

Perhaps a complete reset and returning to qualifying school will be a good thing in the long run for Kiradech Aphibarnrat.

title: Sheehan switches to number eight for Munster derby
article_text:
Leinster captain Dan Sheehan will start at number eight for the first time in Saturday's United Rugby Championship derby against Munster in Dublin.

The Ireland hooker switches to the back row as one of four changes made by head coach Leo Cullen for the Aviva Stadium game (18:00 BST) following last weekend's 48-23 Investec Champions Cup victory over Clermont Auvergne.

Ireland scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park makes his first appearance of the season, while former Munster out-half Joey Carbery earns his first start since rejoining Leinster.

Ronan Kelleher and Jamie Osborne are also drafted into the starting side, with Kelleher replacing Sheehan at hooker and Osborne joining Robbie Henshaw in midfield.

The hosts are seeking consecutive URC victories after bouncing back from opening defeats by the Lions and Sharks with a convincing win over Cardiff.

Leinster have collected eight points from their opening three league matches, including four bonus points.

Munster, meanwhile, have made seven changes to the side that defeated Racing 92 in the Champions Cup last weekend.

Shane Daly returns from injury, while Josh Wycherley, Kieran Brookes, Fineen Wycherley, Jack O'Donoghue, Alex Kendellen and Gavin Coombes are also drafted into the starting XV.

Former Ireland Under-20s international Sean O'Brien switches from the wing to outside centre as he prepares to make his 50th Munster appearance.

Mark Donnelly is in line for his first appearance of the season from the bench, with academy centre Gordon Wood also among the replacements.

Tadhg Beirne and Craig Casey - the only Munster players in Andy Farrell's latest Ireland squad - both start.

Munster have recovered from their opening URC defeat by Glasgow Warriors with a victory over the Bulls and a 26-26 draw against Ulster on October 10.

Leinster: Keenan; T O'Brien, Osborne, Henshaw, J O'Brien; Carbery, Gibson-Park; Porter, Kelleher, Furlong; J McCarthy, Ryan; Baird, Van der Flier, Sheehan (capt).

Replacements: G McCarthy, Usanov, Clarkson, O'Tighearnaigh, Penny, Gunne, Gabriel, Tector.

Replacements: Clein, Donnelly, Ala'alatoa, Edogbo, Gleeson, B O'Donovan, Hanrahan, Wood.

title: Falcons, SIT expand partnership to Spanish market ahead of Madrid game
article_text:
Sports Illustrated Tickets (SIT), the ticketing and fan engagement brand that has swept up partnerships across the NFL in recent seasons, has expanded its agreement with the Atlanta Falcons franchise to cover the team’s upcoming international game in Madrid, Spain.

The Falcons will face the Cincinnati Bengals (another SIT partner) at the iconic 84,000-capacity Santiago Bernabeu stadium on November 8, with SIT to serve as the team's official fan experience partner around the game.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Ahead of the fixture, SIT will offer fans the chance to win tickets to the game through a sweepstakes competition.

SIT has been a partner of the Falcons since the beginning of the 2025 season in a fan experience-focused deal that included the creation of the Sports Illustrated Tickets Lounge hospitality space at the team’s Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Speaking on this new expansion, the vice president of corporate partnerships at Falcons parent AMB Sports and Entertainment, Alex Polofsky, commented: “Sports Illustrated Tickets has been a terrific partner in helping us create memorable experiences for Falcons fans, and we’re excited to extend that relationship internationally as we head to Madrid.

“The NFL’s continued global growth presents incredible opportunities to connect with fans around the world, and this expansion allows us to engage our supporters in Spain in a meaningful way. We look forward to working together to bring the Falcons brand to new audiences and deliver unique opportunities for fans on an international stage.”

SIT is already experienced in the Spanish market, having served as the NFL’s fan engagement partner for its first-ever international game in Madrid in the 2025-26 season.

At that time, SIT chief executive David Lane spoke to Sportcal (GlobalData Sport), explaining: “The game may be held in Madrid, but this is a global event, and a global audience will be tuning in, so it creates increased awareness and opportunities for us as Sports Illustrated Tickets.

“The Spanish market is a focus for us, and we're in active conversations with multiple opportunities and partners there. This [partnership] just helps to start that foundation of what we think is one of the biggest opportunities we see in the world.

“With a partner like the NFL, a stadium [like the Bernabeu], and the team that's responsible for local operations, they are capable of putting on what will be a spectacular game.”

SIT is already an officially licensed NFL ticket vendor through the league’s “open” ticketing system, NFL Ticket HQ.

Recently, it also became the official fan experience partner of the NFL in the UK, in a deal spanning the recent trilogy of London international games.

Having partnered with the league in London this season, and with its partnership with the New England Patriots including the team’s game in Munich, Germany in November, this Spain partnership ensures SIT will feature at five of the six NFL international games in Europe this year.

The Falcons are one of seven NFL teams to partner with SIT, following the New England Patriots, Pittsburgh Steelers, Cincinnati Bengals, Washington Commanders, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and most recently, the Jacksonville Jaguars.

title: Australia call up son of World Cup winner Wilson
article_text:
Teddy Wilson, the son of former Wallabies captain and 1999 Rugby World Cup winner David Wilson, has been named in the Australia squad for November's Nations Championships Tests.

The 24-year-old scrum-half, who captained his country at the 2023 Under-20 World Championships, has been in fine form for the Waratahs and will, along with Tate McDermott, back up first-choice nine Ryan Lonergan.

David Wilson played 79 times for Australia and started at open-side flanker in their World Cup final win over France at Cardiff's Millennium Stadium in 1999.

Teddy revealed that David's jersey from the match is on display at the family home, but added that his father, who moved to Harlequins in 2000 and has subsequently moved into business, has not pushed his children to follow his sporting path.

"Dad doesn't really put much pressure on myself, he's been there and done that, obviously, so he definitely tells me a few things and helps me a lot," said Teddy.

"He just lets me play my game and if he needs to say something, he will."

Wilson is the latest in a series of father-son Wallaby dynasties.

Michael Lynagh's son Tom was Australia's starting fly-half in all three Tests against the British and Irish Lions last year.

Wing Max Jorgensen, prop Angus Bell and hooker Josh Nasser, all named in coach Les Kiss' 33-strong squad alongside Wilson, also had fathers who represented Australia.

Exeter flanker Tom Hooper and Racing 92 prop Taniela Tupou are also included, while centre Len Ikitau, who spent last season at Sandy Park with Hooper, is back from injury.

Australia will play England at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium on Sunday, 8 November, before fixtures against Scotland and Wales on the subsequent weekends.

They will return to Allianz Stadium on the final weekend of November for a play-off against a northern-hemisphere opponent as part of the finale of the new Nations Championship format.

title: Morwenna Talling: 'It’s a bit gutting but it was going to have to come to an end'
article_text:
For many of the current Red Roses players, losing in an England shirt is an unfamiliar feeling.

Last weekend, Canada brought England’s impressive 41-match unbeaten run to an end, as they claimed a thrilling 24-21 victory at BMO Field in Toronto in front of a record-breaking crowd of 18,621 spectators.

For Morwenna Talling, who made her Red Roses debut in 2020 against Italy in a 54-0 win and has been a regular feature in the squad ever since, the defeat marked a rare low in an England career largely defined by success, but she is determined to help England bounce back when the two sides meet again in the WXV Global Series this weekend.

“Obviously we’ve gone through a massive streak and I’ve had the opportunity to play with this team having never lost,” Talling said.

“It’s a bit gutting but it was going to have to come to an end and I’m so grateful to have been a part of that period of time when we did win all those games.

“It just shows how much the rest of the rugby world is coming along and it’s only going to make the game better and grow everyone individually and as a team.”

Rather than focusing on the end of their winning streak, England now have the opportunity to try and level their three-Test series with Canada and Talling is embracing the challenge of experiencing something new with her side.

“We have the chance to go again this weekend and see what we can give,” she said.

“We’ve always had the opportunity to win and then go on and back that win up with another win. This time it’s different.

“It allows us to respond to something we’ve never responded to before.”

The back row continued, “Naturally that changes what we do in camp. Our processes stay the same, but you can feel that shift of knowing we’ve got to respond and try and go win.

“Being able to execute when we go score and finish the pressure we build is probably the biggest thing going into this weekend.

“I think we did have that pressure on Canada, but we let ourselves down in that area. We’ve picked up a few areas we need to work on.

“We know what we do does work, so it’s just that execution piece. It’s our chance to respond and we’re all definitely looking forward to it.”

While England look to improve on the pitch, the 24-year-old highlighted the importance of keeping the squad connected off it.

“As a group we’ve bonded really well. We went out for dinner last night and we’ve got an ice hockey game tonight, which we’re going to go see altogether as a group,” she said with a smile.

“I think that it’s really important to stick to that and keep bonding.”

Talling also stressed the value of facing the best opposition regularly, with the WXV Global Series providing England with the chance to test themselves against Canada three times, as well as Australia and the Black Ferns and they still have the USA to go on October 30.

“We always want to challenge ourselves against the best and to be able to do that pretty much six weeks in a row is something that you don’t normally get to do.

“To have that opportunity to test our game, test where we’re at and do it against Canada three times makes us evolve and makes every team better,” she added.

“Canada have grown a lot. They’ve always been a physical side, but they’ve taken that to another level. Their backs were crazy good the other day and they’ve got absolute pace in the wide channel.

“Their overall game has developed and they’re continuing to grow, so we’ve just got to keep growing above that.

“Similar to the other countries going to do different parts of the world, it’s testing everyone against harder competition. I think it’s needed and we’re really looking forward to the challenge.”

The Red Roses will face Canada at TD Place in Ottawa in their third and final Test against the side this Friday.

title: Rafael Nadal leads tributes as star who beat him, Djokovic, Federer & Alcaraz retires from tennis
article_text:
Rafael Nadal, Grigor Dimitrov and Richard Gasquet led the tributes to David Goffin after the Belgian star retired from tennis in Brussels.

In the final match of his career, Goffin was beaten 6-3, 6-4 by world No 37 Alex Michelsen in the second round of the ATP 250 tournament on Thursday.

During an illustrious career, Goffin amassed a 358-276 record and won six ATP Tour titles, while he was a runner-up at the 2017 ATP Finals and the 2019 Cincinnati Masters. He was also a four-time Grand Slam quarter-finalist, and he helped Belgium reach the Davis Cup final in 2015 and 2017.

The 35-year-old reached a career-high ranking of world No 7, which makes him the only Belgian man to be ranked in the top 10.

Goffin earned 21 wins against top 10 players, including multiple victories over Nadal, Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev, as well as triumphs against Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer and Stan Wawrinka.

Speaking to ATPTour.com after his last match, Goffin said: “I’m proud of all my career. I gave everything to try to reach my goals.

“I’m proud of the attitude that I always had in front of the difficulties that I had in my career. I’m proud of the wins I had, the opponents I beat.

“A lot of things I’m really proud of. But in the end, I have no regrets and I gave everything until the very end.

“A younger version of myself would say that it’s quite a good career, quite good emotions with the impressive places that I played, like a stadium with a crowd, the Davis Cup ties that I played. Hopefully a younger David would be impressed.”

After his match with Michelsen, Goffin’s career was celebrated in an on-court ceremony, and tributes recorded by several tennis stars were played on the big screen.

The montage started with a video from 22-time Grand Slam champion Nadal, who had some kinds words for Goffin.

“Hello David. How are you doing, man? I just want to congratulate you on your amazing career,” Nadal said.

“It has been a huge pleasure to share practices, matches, great moments together on the tour.”

Retired French star Gasquet followed Nadal.

“David, this video is to congratulate you in your great career,” the former world No 7 said.

“It has been an honour to share this time with you. You are truly an extraordinary person and an extraordinary player.”

Former world No 3 Dimitrov, who played Goffin 11 times, said: “Congratulations on your incredible career and amazing journey, my dear friend.

“Thank you for sharing the court with me for so many years.”

Goffin extended his career by defeating Remy Bartola 3-6, 6-3, 6-4 in the first round of the European Open on Wednesday.

After battling back from 0-3 down in the third set against Bartola, an emotional Goffin said: “I don’t know what to say, it was one of the toughest moments and nicest moments when I came on the court.

“The first few games were really tough for me with the nerves. Then I started to serve well. Most important is the support that the crowd gave me in the whole match… It is the best feeling we can have.”

Following his last ATP Tour victory, Goffin admitted he had to cancel his plans.

“I’m going to have to cancel the evening I had booked,” Goffin was quoted as saying by L’Equipe.

“It was both the best and the toughest entrance I’ve ever experienced. I was very nervous, and the most important thing was the support of the crowd from the first point to the last.

“Finishing the match with a winning shot was huge. Everything was perfect.”

title: Carlos Alcaraz adds another ATP tournament to 2027 calendar despite schedule complaints
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has been very vocal about his displeasure at the gruelling nature of the ATP Tour since returning to action after his wrist injury.

The star missed four and a half months of action between April and August, before he made his return at the 2026 US Open.

Since, he’s opened up about playing less tournaments going forward to combat the hectic tennis schedule and his fitness worries.

At the Shanghai Masters, Alcaraz said: “One of the reasons we had to see the players who are getting injured, they [ATP officials] are pushing us too much out of the line sometimes to play a lot of tournaments, to play a lot of matches.

“It’s getting in the wrong direction,” he continued before turning his attention towards Jannik Sinner’s decision to end his season early. “I just wish Jannik the best for these months, just to be in good shape for the next season.”

Despite Alcaraz’s complaints, the Spaniard has added yet another ATP 500 tournament to his growing calendar.

Alcaraz is already confirmed for the Rotterdam Open in February and now he has been confirmed to play Queen’s in London during the grass court swing.

Queen’s is one of the tournaments Alcaraz was forced to miss due to his wrist injury and he has a very good record at the tournament.

The Spaniard has lifted the title at Queen’s on two occasions, in 2023 and 2025, and he has only every suffered one defeat at the London event.

That came against Jack Draper in 2024, who beat the Spaniard in straight sets in the second round of the tournament.

It should be no surprise that Alcaraz has already bolstered his grass court schedule for 2026, where he is also basically guaranteed to play Wimbledon.

Alcaraz has built a superb record on grass over the years, despite playing a limited amount of the surface.

He holds an incredible 35-4 record on the surface since his debut, which equates to a magnificent 90% winning rate on grass.

That’s helped him win Wimbledon twice, in 2023 and 2024, and reached a further final in 2025. The only player to beat Alcaraz in the last four years at Wimbledon is Jannik Sinner, who won the 2025 final against the Spaniard.

As for Queen’s, the ATP 500 tournament was won by Francisco Cerundolo in 2026 in the absence of Alcaraz, who beat Tommy Paul in the London final.

Next year’s Queen’s event is set to take place between the 5th and the 20th June, with the men’s tournament taking place in the second week of action.

title: Warren Gatland issues denial, confirms English offer and shares big family news
article_text:
Warren Gatland has denied he applied for the Fiji head coach role, despite reports in the country that he was desperately close to getting the job.

Reports in Fiji claimed that Gatland was one of the favoured candidates, alongside the man eventually hired - former Springbok boss Jake White. As well as the reports in Fiji, sources close to the appointment process said that Gatland was believed to have applied.

The speculation grew so intense that Fijian players had reportedly been informed he was getting the job.

However, that was short-lived, with White getting the job just a day after those reports.

And the former Wales coach has now distanced himself from the official application process, saying he only held talks with Fiji's governing body.

"I did speak to them and then I just said, look, I'm not going to follow through with applying for the job," Gatland told Boyle Sports, who offer rugby odds.

"I mean look, they're an exciting team. I think Jake White will do a good job with them. You feel like with a team like that there's a lot of things you can do to improve on, but yeah, it's just the timing wasn't quite right.

"I had a grandson born a couple of weeks ago now, a third grandchild, and we had just settled. If something else came along and I felt it was the right thing, I would look at something."

Gatland had previously been linked with Gallagher Prem club Harlequins earlier this year, as a director of rugby at the Stoop.

However, that didn't materialise amid reports that Gatland wasn't keen to take on the bulk of the coaching.

"I did speak to Harlequins during the year," added Gatland. "They made me an offer, but the timing wasn't quite right.

"It's a club that I've always had a bit of time for - they've got a pool of players to develop from in terms of youngsters.

"That would have been potentially exciting, but just the timing wasn't quite right for me.

"Maybe a club role [would appeal] or something like that. International rugby is really tough because I don't think people appreciate the limited preparation time.

"You've got basically five or six training sessions, you're playing an international, and people expect you to win.

"The good thing about club stuff is that you've almost got an opportunity to experiment and fail to succeed.

"You can try things and it doesn't quite work out. You don't have that luxury in international rugby."

Gatland has not held a permanent role since leaving the Wales coaching job for the second time midway through the 2025 Six Nations, after overseeing 14 consecutive defeats - eventually being replaced by Steve Tandy.

title: Former Scotland Rugby International Tim Visser to Stand Trial on Rape and Abuse Charges
article_text:
Former Scotland rugby international Tim Visser is set to stand trial after being accused of rape and abusive behaviour towards a woman.

The 39-year-old faces four charges relating to alleged incidents between 2010 and 2024.

Two charges allege that Visser raped the woman on various occasions.

He also faces allegations of threatening, controlling and abusive behaviour.

The charges include claims of physical violence and controlling aspects of the woman's daily life.

His defence lawyer, Ian Duguid, entered a plea of not guilty on his behalf.

A trial has been scheduled to begin in Edinburgh on 12 January 2028.

Born in the Netherlands, Visser chose to represent Scotland at international level.

The winger made 33 appearances for Scotland between 2012 and 2017.

He also played club rugby for Newcastle Falcons, Edinburgh and Harlequins before retiring in 2019.

The allegations have not been proven in court, and Visser denies the charges.

title: Midnite secures snooker Triple Crown with UK Championship sponsorship
article_text:
The sportsbook and casino operator now sponsors all three of snooker’s top global tournaments.

Midnite has added the UK Championship to its snooker sponsorship portfolio, meaning it now has partnerships with each of the sport’s top three events.

The casino and sportsbook operator initially partnered with the World Championship in 2025 before adding the Masters to its roster.

The company’s extended agreement with the World Snooker Tour now includes a betting and casino partnership with the third Triple Crown event.

The deal starts in the current season, with the UK Championship held between November 28 and December 6 at the Barbican in York, England.

Callum Wilson, senior PR manager at Midnite, said: "Snooker has been a fantastic sport for us to be involved with, and we're really excited to be extending our partnership with the World Snooker Tour to cover all three Triple Crown events.

“We've already had some great experiences working with WST through the World Championship and the Masters, so adding the UK Championship feels like a natural next step for us.

"These are the three tournaments that every snooker player dreams of winning, and they mean a huge amount to fans as well. To have Midnite involved in all three is something we're really proud of.

"We've enjoyed building our relationship with WST and we're excited to keep that going, finding new ways to get involved in the sport and bring fans closer to the action."

Midnite continues to ramp up its promotional activity, with its snooker expansion the latest deal after a deal with the NFL in the UK and Ireland.

The operator also has a strong presence in UK football, with the likes of Wolverhampton Wanderers.

title: Two Circles Appoints Media Rights Veteran Augustine Tan to Lead APAC Expansion
article_text:
Global sports and entertainment agency Two Circles has officially appointed industry veteran Augustine Tan as Head of Media Rights for the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region, targeting an aggressive commercial expansion across one of the world’s most dynamic media landscapes.

Announced on Tuesday, 20 October 2026, the strategic hire comes as Two Circles looks to bolster its regional rights business, combining audience data analytics, streaming capabilities, and live production assets to assist rights holders in unlocking greater commercial returns from their broadcast content.

Tan brings over two decades of senior sports media rights experience to the role. He previously held high-profile leadership positions at SPORTFIVE, WWE, and Perform/DAZN, overseeing commercial distribution and rights partnerships for tier-one sports properties including FIBA, the WTA, and the NFL. Most recently, Tan operated his own independent sports media consultancy, A Side Project 2022, advising high-profile clients such as World Rugby, Dentsu, and LFCTV on regional distribution strategies.

In his new position, Tan will lead Two Circles’ media rights operations across APAC, driving revenue growth across diverse markets, platforms, and fan bases. The executive appointment builds on the agency’s growing global momentum, following its recently secured partnership extension with the International Skating Union (ISU).

Highlighting the scale of the commercial opportunity across the region, Tan emphasised the role of data-driven insights in capturing market share.

title: College Sports Media Rights Bill Awaits House Action
article_text:
Most Division I college athletics programs spend more than they generate, and a new Congressional Research Service (CRS) report examines whether Congress should intervene in college sports media rights, conference realignment and production facility funding, or leave colleges to govern themselves.

The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that 94% of Division I schools, 330 of 352, spent more on athletics than they generated in revenue in the 2023–2024 academic year.

The Protect College Sports Act of 2026, sponsored by Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX), passed the Senate on Sept. 28.

Football Bowl Subdivision (FBS) schools collectively spent $13.06 billion on athletics in 2025 and generated $13.03 billion in revenue, according to the Knight-Newhouse College Athletics Database. GAO estimated that Power Four college sports media rights revenue of $2.3 billion in 2023–2024 was nearly as large as the combined athletics revenue of all other Division I colleges, at $3.1 billion. That concentration shapes the report's central policy question: whether a statutory antitrust exemption would let schools bargain collectively and stabilize finances, or whether federal intervention would introduce new complications.

The report traces the current structure to NCAA v. Board of Regents of the University of Oklahoma, 468 U.S. 85 (1984), in which the Supreme Court held that the NCAA's television rights policies violated Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890. Since that ruling, Power Four conferences have used a "granting of rights" model, under which member schools sign their media rights over to the conference in exchange for a share of revenue.

The Protect College Sports Act, as amended by Sen. John Thune's substitute amendment, would create a "covered entity" with an antitrust exemption to collectively negotiate college sports media rights, if schools voluntarily join and the entity includes at least 75% of FBS schools. Title III of the bill would authorize $180 million annually for fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2032 for competitive grants to help historically Black colleges and universities invest in broadband, media production and sports broadcasting infrastructure.

The report also notes that scheduling a College Football Playoff game on the second Saturday of December would conflict with Executive Order 14396, signed March 20, which directs that no postseason college football game be broadcast in a way that directly conflicts with the Army-Navy Game; a provision in the bill as amended would codify that protection in statute.

The Senate passed S. 4668 on Sept. 28 by a 77–22 vote. The House held the bill at the desk on Oct. 5. Unresolved questions include whether the 75% membership threshold is achievable and how a free local telecast requirement might affect media payments.

The report notes that the true costs of college sports may be higher than current estimates, because the expenses tracked by Knight-Newhouse and GAO may not reflect capital expenditures schools incur to meet media production requirements.
